item.title: ‘Slow down the internet a little’: Quader-Palak conversation played at Tribunal
item.description:
Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader instructed that internet speeds be slowed during the July Mass Uprising, with the directive approved by ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and implemented by then State Minister for Information and Communication Technology Zunaid Ahmed Palak.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim made the claims while presenting closing arguments in the case concerning crimes against humanity allegedly committed during the July Mass Uprising.

He presented arguments for the third consecutive day on Sunday before International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury.

The other two members of the three-member tribunal are Judge Md Manjurul Bashid and Judge Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir.

Early in Sunday’s proceedings, the tribunal played an audio recording of a telephone conversation between Obaidul Quader and Zunaid Ahmed Palak. In the recording, Quader is heard saying, “Slow down the internet a little.”

Palak replies, “Shall I get permission from the Leader?”

“Get it,” Quader responds.

Palak then says, “You know, it has been said that unless she says...” Quader subsequently instructs him to ask Sheikh Hasina and then slow down the internet.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar told the tribunal that the telephone conversation between Quader and Palak was not merely an exchange of words and that the prosecution had established its significance through documentary evidence.

A document from the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) states that internet services were suspended or restricted following verbal instructions from then State Minister Zunaid Ahmed Palak.

It further says Palak informed the BTRC that the measures had been implemented on the instructions of the Ministry of Home Affairs and on the basis of information provided by various intelligence agencies.

According to the list of measures recorded in the document, at 6:39 pm on 16 July 2024, instructions were issued to suspend 3G and 4G network services at 1,153 sites across 55 public universities and four private universities—59 universities in total.

The document was subsequently submitted for retrospective approval of the network shutdown measures, taking all relevant circumstances into consideration. It bears the signatures of the then BTRC director general and other officials concerned.

The other accused in the case, apart from Obaidul Quader, are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim; former State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat; Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan; and Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif.

All the accused in the case are absconding.

item.title: PM hands over keys of new houses to flood-hit families in Banshkhali
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday handed over keys of newly built houses to families, whose homes were destroyed in the recent floods in Banshkhali upazila of Chattogram.

The prime minister handed over the keys to the beneficiaries after visiting the flood-affected Paschim Banshkhali area under Baharchhara Union at around 1:20 pm as part of his programme to rehabilitate the flood-hit people.

During his visit, the prime minister also talked to the affected people and inquired about the wellbeing of their families. Later, he also planted a ‘mahogany’ sapling in the area.

Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Disaster Management and Relief Minister Asadul Habib Dulu and other senior officials accompanied the prime minister.

Later, the prime minister attended a programme titled “House Handover, Grant and Relief Materials Distribution” at the Banshkhali High School and College ground, organised for the rehabilitation of families affected by the recent floods in Chattogram.

Under the government rehabilitation initiative, 100 flood-affected families in Banshkhali were selected to receive the keys of the newly built houses.

Earlier, 100 affected families had been identified to receive the houses, which were constructed with government funding using RCC pillars, wood and corrugated iron sheets to make them more resilient to natural disasters, with each house having two rooms and an attached toilet.

Heavy rain and hill runoff since 7 July inundated several remote and low-lying areas of Banshkhali, damaging homes and affecting fish farms, ponds and other water bodies.

The prime minister earlier visited Matarbari in Maheshkhali to inspect development activities, including the Matarbari deep-sea port and coal-fired power project.

After completing his Banshkhali programme, the prime minister is scheduled to travel to Fatikchhari, where he will meet Hefazat-e-Islam Ameer Allama Shah Muhibullah Babunagari at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Ulum Babunagar Madrasah.

He will later visit Hathazari and attend another rehabilitation programme for flood victims at Hathazari Government College ground at 5:00 pm.

In the evening, the prime minister will attend an organisational meeting at the auditorium of Radisson Blu Chattogram Bay View hotel in Chattogram.

After completing his engagements, the prime minister is scheduled to return to Dhaka by a flight from Hazrat Shah Amanat International Airport at 9:30 pm.

The visit marks Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s first trip to Maheshkhali, Fatikchhari and Hathazari after assuming office.

Salman Shah murder case: Actor Don arrested
item.description:
Actor Ashraful Haque, popularly known as Don, who is known for playing antagonist roles in films, has been arrested in connection with the murder case involving popular film actor Salman Shah.

Don was arrested at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Sunday afternoon.

Kamrul Hasan Talukder, Officer-in-Charge of the Airport police station, told Prothom Alo that immigration police arrested Don before a team from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) took him into custody.

The CID is investigating the case in which he was arrested, he added.

Jasim Uddin, Special Superintendent of Police (Media) at the CID, told Prothom Alo that Don was arrested at the airport with the assistance of immigration police in connection with the Salman Shah murder case. He was subsequently sent to court.

A court ordered the filing of a murder case last year, 29 years after Salman Shah’s death. Later, the lawsuit was lodged.

item.title: Afghanistan's gold rush upends lives and landscapes
item.description:
AFGHANISTAN-ECONOMY-ENVIRONMENT-MINING

In Afghanistan's northeastern Badakhshan province, dozens of excavators operate day and night to extract gold from the mountains where villagers and their livestock once roamed.

Thousands of miners are deployed across the Shiwa area, about 50 kilometres (30 miles) northeast of the provincial capital Faizabad, extracting gold for investors nationwide.

Some residents in the area have profited from the gold rush, only to regret it later, such as farmer Muhammad Amin.

"Before, the river was deep, the water was clean," said the 74-year-old from Pul-e-Ziri Ban valley.

Since mining got underway, "the water of the river is not drinkable; you can't even wash your body with that water", he told AFP.

With tears in his eyes, Amin said the grass along the riverbank "has all gone" and farming is no longer possible due to "the wind and dust".

Now he can only feed up to 15 goats, compared with as many as 40 previously.

Amin said he was paid half the USD 20,000 for which he agreed to lease his land to a mining firm that failed to fulfil a promise to restore his fields after the work stopped.

The Taliban authorities have expanded the mining sector since returning to power five years ago, aiming to tap into Afghanistan's vast underground resources to boost state coffers.

Abdul Mateen Rahimzai, head of Badakhshan's mines department, said they have registered "almost 650 to 700 companies, and there are thousands of people working manually".

The World Bank said hundreds of mining contracts have been signed since 2021, with "real growth averaging 25 to 30 percent" annually according to a May report.

'Better than anything else'

While mining has temporarily stopped in Amin's village, not far from his home, in Gulak-Dara valley, dozens of diggers were carving into the mountainside.

With jobs scarce in Afghanistan, the area has drawn workers from across the country.

Mohammad Agha Khwaja Khail, from Kabul, has worked in mining for five years and earns 10,000 Afghanis (USD 150) a month loading trucks.

"It's better than anything else... There aren't many jobs in Kabul," said the 21-year-old, above the din of diggers.

Shafiullah Ehsas, a father-of-five, transported his excavator hundreds of kilometres from Jalalabad about three months ago.

"In Jalalabad, the gold (mining) work hasn't started, and it was happening in Badakhshan, so we didn't have any other option but to bring our machinery here," said the 32-year-old, who earns 25,000 Afghanis per month.

The Ministry of Mines and Petroleum has sought to regulate the industry, with spokesman Hamayoun Afghan saying resources "used to be extracted erratically; it wasn't done under supervision" by the previous government.

Gold mining has accelerated in the north, the ministry spokesman said, including in neighbouring Takhar province where an Afghan company was operating with Chinese partners.

Fabrizio Foschini, a researcher at the Afghanistan Analysts Network, said during earlier decades of war "mining mainly benefited insurgent groups, including the Taliban, and local strongmen with links to corrupt government officials".

Mining firms are now taxed 20 grams of gold per hectare per month, or the equivalent in cash, no matter their profits.

'Reduced to ruins'

Mohammadullah Mubariz, the manager of a mining company with about a hundred labourers and 20 diggers, said the team can extract "200 to 300 grams of gold" in a week.

Despite this, he said the firm was operating at a loss because of start-up costs since April.

Rahimzai, head of the provincial mines department, said last year the government collected 112 kilograms (247 pounds) of gold in Badakhshan. According to miners who spoke to AFP, their sale price per gram was around USD 118.

Rahimzai said that last year, "most of the mines were not registered, and there was no system to collect the fees from them".

He has also ordered the closure of around 225 sites that caused damage, including in the Shiwa area.

"There was a bridge there, there were shops, and there was a school. All of them were buried under floodwater, mud, and debris. The area has been completely reduced to ruins," Rahimzai told AFP.

The provincial mining chief also pledged to tackle any corruption, and ensure the "mineral resources of Badakhshan will be utilised properly and for the benefit of the people".

Some parts of the province remain untouched, including a few kilometres from Shiwa where herder Fazil hoped the miners would stay away.

"Because it's a place for people, for picnics, for livestock to graze," he told AFP, giving only his first name for security reasons.

The gold industry "doesn't benefit the local communities here", said the 45-year-old, who has brought his herd to the mountains each summer since childhood.

"It benefits only the powerful people."

Problems solved when we talk: Dinesh Trivedi
item.description:
India’s High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, has expressed optimism about resolving problems through dialogue.

He said that problems are solved when the two sides talk to each other.

The Indian High Commissioner made the remarks in response to questions from journalists on Sunday afternoon at the inauguration of a children’s playground at the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC) in Jamuna Future Park in the capital.

Prime Minister almost certain not to attend BRICS summit

Asked about his courtesy meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman scheduled for Monday, Dinesh Trivedi said, “We all have great respect for Bangladesh’s prime minister. I have heard his speeches many times. He is a people-friendly person. Our prime minister is also a people-friendly person.”

The Indian High Commissioner said when the two leaders meet, a lot of problems will be solved.

“Problems are sorted out when we talk to each other. I firmly believe that the people are one. There will be a solution. There is nothing negative here. Everything is positive,” he said.

item.title: Withdraw cash by tapping cards at ATMs, no fear of card getting stuck
item.description:
Many people face the inconvenience of having their cards retained by ATMs while trying to withdraw cash. To address the problem, contactless ATM services using Near Field Communication (NFC) technology have been introduced in Bangladesh.

Private commercial bank City Bank has launched this new facility, which will be available at its ATM booths. However, customers of other banks will also be able to enjoy this facility.

With the new technology, customers can withdraw and deposit money and conduct other banking transactions at ATMs simply by tapping their cards, without inserting them into the machine. An NFC-enabled ATM card may be required for the service. All banks are now issuing cards compatible with the technology.

City Bank claims to be the only bank in Bangladesh to have introduced ATMs equipped with this technology.

How it works

At conventional ATM booths, the plastic card has to be inserted into the machine's slot and a PIN number must be entered. With this service, the card often gets stuck inside the machine. The risk is higher when using a specific bank's card at another bank's ATM.

With an NFC-enabled ATM, there is no need to insert the card into the machine. Customers simply tap the card on a designated area of the ATM, which then identifies the card. They can enter their PIN and complete the transaction quickly and securely.

City Bank has already installed 70 to 80 ATMs equipped with the new technology. The bank plans to install NFC-enabled machines whenever it adds or replaces ATMs in the future.

Although the service has been added to City Bank’s ATM network, customers of any bank in Bangladesh will be able to use it. Under the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB) system, customers of one bank can use ATMs operated by other banks. An additional Tk 15 is charged for each such transaction.

What are the benefits

Cards can sometimes get stuck inside ATMs because of power outages or technical problems. As the card does not need to be inserted into the machine with contactless technology, there is no risk of it getting stuck or being retained by the ATM.

Traditional ATMs were also vulnerable to card-data theft through ‘skimming devices’ that could copy information from a card’s magnetic stripe. With NFC technology, the card exchanges information by transmitting signals directly, which, according to City Bank officials, makes the possibility of cloning or data theft extremely low.

The technology also saves the additional time required to read the card and eject it after a transaction, reducing the overall time needed for a transaction, bank officials said. Repeated insertion into ATM slots can also wear down a card’s magnetic stripe and EMV chip. The new system helps keep the card intact.

City Bank Deputy Managing Director Arup Haider told Prothom Alo, “The new technology-based ATMs have been introduced for customers’ convenience. Customers will be able to conduct transactions quickly and comfortably without inserting their cards into the ATM.”

item.title: PM: Stay alert to attempts to create chaos
Swapon: Media must accurately reflect society
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon has said the media is a mirror of society and must accurately reflect how society functions.
“The media is the mirror of society. How society functions should be reflected in the media. The mirror of the media must be flawless,” he said.
The minister made the remarks as the chief guest at a program marking the 56th anniversary of Dainik Biplobi Bangladesh, a newspaper published from Barisal, at Ashwini Kumar Hall in the Sadar Road area of the city on Sunday.
“A media with flaws will not be able to portray the real face of society. Therefore, the responsibility for making the media flawless must be taken by the media itself. Otherwise, the media will lose its credibility,” he said.
Swapon said the media must also play the role of a watchdog to ensure that all political parties remain committed to changing the country’s political culture.
“If journalists collectively conduct investigative reports, identify the sources of drugs and those involved in the trade, and expose influential people involved in crime, society or politics, it will become much easier for the state to take action,” he said.
The minister said a deep conspiracy is underway to keep the future generation addicted to drugs.
“The future generation is being targeted, while Bangladesh is also being used as a market. We have also seen that some MPs of the previous Awami League government from border areas amassed assets worth crores of taka through the illegal drug trade.
Following the change of government, those involved in the trade are now seeking partners within the current ruling party. Such important information can only be brought to light by the media,” he said.
On development, the minister said development should no longer be measured by mega projects, massive buildings or large, expensive vehicles.
“Development now does not mean mega projects, huge visible buildings or large vehicles that can be touched. Today’s development is the gas resources hidden beneath the ground—resources that the previous government could not or did not extract during its 17 years in power,” he said.
He alleged that the country’s electricity system and infrastructure had been made dependent on an import-based energy policy by importing fuel from abroad at costs thousands of times higher than domestic extraction costs, in order to benefit importers.
“Beyond the foreign currency we earn through ready-made garment exports and the foreign currency received through remittances, we do not have many sources of foreign currency earnings.
How ruthless and greedy must a government be to conspire to make such a weak economy dependent on imports just to make a group of looters rich?” he said, referring to the previous Awami League government.
The minister said the previous government chose to import gas instead of extracting domestic gas because there was less opportunity for profit from extraction.
“The previous government did not extract gas and instead opted for imports because the profit is lower when gas is extracted.
It is not possible to create middlemen in this process. But the current government is giving the highest priority to gas extraction.
The government will import only as much gas as is necessary to sustain the electricity infrastructure.
We will try to meet the rest through domestic extraction. This will make it possible to reduce costs,” he said.
Speaking about political reform, Swapon said the country needed a new political settlement.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has announced a 31-point program for this new political settlement. Through that program, we want to repair Bangladesh.
We want to reform Bangladesh,” he said.
“The culture of godfathers and musclemen will not be encouraged in the BNP. Political leaders and activists whose words themselves create an unpleasant impression and who cannot speak properly should not be given a place in the BNP,” he said.
He said the media must play a “whip-like role” so that political parties are compelled to take responsibility for changing the country’s political culture.
The program was presided over by Nurul Alam Farid, freedom fighter, publisher and editor of Dainik Biplobi Bangladesh.
Among others, Barisal Press Club President Aminul Islam Khasru, BNP leader Azizul Haque Akkas, former member secretary of Barisal Metropolitan BNP Mir Zahidul Kabir Zahid, freedom fighter Israel Pandit, Barisal Sadar Upazila BNP Convener Nurul Amin, freedom fighter Ebaydul Haque Chand, Barisal Metropolitan BNP Joint Convener Afroza Khanam Nasrin and district Mahila Dal President Fatema Rahman were present at the event.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Science toys, math labs planned for primary schools
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj on Sunday said science toys and various hands-on learning materials will be introduced in the primary school curriculum to make children’s learning more enjoyable and practical.
The government is also taking an initiative to introduce math labs in primary schools, where students will learn basic mathematical concepts such as shapes, sizes, multiplication, division, addition and subtraction through practical activities and learning materials, he said while addressing a programme titled “Foundational Learning Action Tracker” organized by UNICEF Bangladesh at a city hotel.
The state minister said greater emphasis is being placed on science, mathematics, design and creativity in primary education.
Highlighting the need to address gaps in foundational learning, he said one of the most important goals of primary education is to ensure that every child develops basic reading, writing and mathematical skills.
Regarding out-of-school children, Bobby Hajjaj said the government is implementing various programmes to bring children who are currently outside the education system into school.
He said initiatives have also been taken to provide various forms of support, including free school uniforms, to help children stay in school.
The first-ever free school uniform distribution program will be inaugurated on August 16, the state minister said.
Regarding the mid-day meal program, he said steps have been taken to address the shortcomings and limitations identified during implementation of the pilot project.
Primary and Mass Education Secretary Jasmin Nahar, UNICEF Bangladesh Representative Rana Flowers and Director General of the Directorate of Primary Education Shahina Ferdousi, among others, attended the program.

item.title: Indian high commissioner meets foreign minister
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi had a meeting with Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman at a state guest house on Sunday.
"I can only tell you it's a pre-arranged meeting, and I don't know what they discussed," a senior official aware of the meeting told UNB.
Fresh tensions have surfaced between Dhaka and New Delhi following former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s recent speech in New Delhi, with her remarks drawing strong reactions in Bangladesh.
On Thursday, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam reiterated that Dhaka wants constructive engagement with New Delhi, noting that the two neighbours have a wide range of bilateral issues requiring continued dialogue.
"We want our relations... because we have many issues with India, many bilateral issues - water, energy, and the border - that need to be resolved through discussion and dialogue," she said.
Shama Obaed, however, emphasized that Bangladesh's relationship with India extends far beyond the current issue.
"A country has many aspects to its relationship with another country. We need to have a lot of dialogue with them, and we need to hold discussions. We have cooperation on energy, we have a major issue with them over water, and there are issues on the border - these have to be resolved through discussions," she said.

item.title: HC order barring Khairul Haque’s arrest without specific case upheld
item.description:
The Appellate Division on Sunday upheld a High Court order directing authorities not to arrest or harass former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque without a specific case against him.
A four-member Appellate Division bench led by the Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury passed the order while disposing of a state petition challenging the High Court order.
Lawyers said the HC order remains applicable to Khairul Haque, meaning he cannot be arrested or harassed without being shown arrested in a specific case.
Senior lawyers Kamrul Haque Siddiqui, Sara Hossain, Mostafizur Rahman Khan, Mahbub Shafique and Monayem Nabi Shahin argued for the petitioner. Deputy Attorney General Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury represented the state.
On May 17, a High Court bench comprising Justice Razik-Al-Jalil and Justice Debashish Roy Chowdhury issued the order along with a rule.
Earlier, on May 12, Khairul Haque secured bail from the High Court in two cases filed over killings during the July uprising. His lawyers had said there was no legal impediment to his release as he had obtained bail in all the cases against him. The state later appealed against the order.
On April 28, the Appellate Division upheld his bail in five cases filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), as well as cases over the killing of a Jubo Dal activist during the July uprising and alleged forgery of a caretaker government verdict.
Earlier, on March 8, the High Court granted him bail in four cases after making the relevant rules absolute. He was also granted bail in an ACC case on March 11. The Appellate Division later dismissed the state’s plea seeking to stay the bail orders.
Khairul Haque was subsequently shown arrested in the Arif murder case filed with Jatrabari Police Station and the Rubel murder case filed with Adabor Police Station. After lower courts rejected his bail pleas, he moved the High Court and secured bail in both cases on May 12. He faces seven cases in total.
Khairul Haque was arrested from his Dhanmondi residence in Dhaka on July 24, 2025, and later shown arrested in a case over the killing of Juba Dal activist Abdul Qayyum Ahad during the July movement.

item.title: Fakhrul: Small humanitarian initiatives can bring about big changes
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said it is possible to bring about big changes in the lives of underprivileged people through small humanitarian and social initiatives. “Not only financial assistance, but also creating opportunities for helpless people to stand on their own feet by making them work-oriented is the most important thing,” he said. He said this while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony of the "Self-reliance Project for the Underprivileged" initiated by the US-based charity organization "Love Share BD" at the city’s District Shilpokola Academy Auditorium on Sunday. He handed over 25 "Tea Houses" to 25 underprivileged people of the Rangpur region under the project to make them self-reliant. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, also the ruling BNP Secretary General, said that although this initiative of "Love Share BD" to make these 25 underprivileged people self-reliant today is small in number, it can bring about big changes in their lives. Calling for working unitedly to rise above political divisions for the development of the backward people of Rangpur division, he said that local leaders should play an effective role in ensuring the self-reliance of the people of their respective areas. The minister said that the BNP government is committed to the people's fate and is working towards that goal. “The present government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is trying to revamp the country's ruined economy and troubled administration. These cannot be implemented so quickly. We do not have any Aladdin's lamp in our hands,” he said. Mirza Fakhrul said: "We have an opposition party. Unfortunately, they have started playing the same role as before. They are also speaking the same language that Sheikh Hasina used to speak. Such politics are not good for the country.” He advised the opposition party to talk if the BNP government, which has received the majority mandate from the people only some five months ago, fails to run the country. “In the words of the opposition party, it has to be done right now although no development is possible in a day,” he said.
The minister said that the opportunity to build the country has come after the end of the fascist regime. Stating that during the fascist era, cases were filed against six million people, 20,000 people were killed, and 1,700 people fell victim to enforced disappearance, that situation does not exist in the country now. Regarding the country's development activities, Mirza Fakhrul said that the government is implementing various programs to revive the economy, increase agriculture and employment, and improve the living standards of the common people. He also highlighted various initiatives taken to develop agriculture and irrigation systems, create employment, and address the energy crisis. “The country has an energy problem. The Awami League government has not explored a single gas and oil mine in the country in the last 15 years. They crippled BAPEX. After taking charge, we are trying to dig oil and gas wells in the country,” he said. The minister said oil and gas have to be imported from abroad. Its price has increased by billions of dollars in the international market, he said, adding that due to the war between Iran and the United States, oil and gas imports have suffered a loss of four billion dollars. “However, the people of the country have not been without oil and gas for a single day. The supply has decreased slightly, but there has been no extreme crisis. The crisis that exists in the country will be resolved in a short time,” he added. At this time, he also commented that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's pre-election promises are being implemented step by step. Mirza Fakhrul Islam claimed that a lot has changed in four to five months. The government is carrying out reform activities in various sectors to meet the expectations of the people, he said. He also commented that time and everyone's cooperation are needed to implement these initiatives. Addressing the media, he said: "Even though we could not write during the Awami League era, now we can write both truth and lies. Now, democracy has been established in the country, and opportunities have been created to speak in parliament.” Speaking as a special guest, Senior Secretary to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and journalist Mushfiqul Fazal Ansarey urged people concerned not to use power as a money-making machine. “It is a commendable example that 'Love Share BD' entrepreneurs are standing by the backward people by spending their own money. Although the scope of such initiatives is small, its purpose is very noble,” he said. Director of "Love Share BD" Zahid Khan said that the organization's activities have started from the real experience of people's helplessness and poverty.
“Our main goal is not only to help the disadvantaged people, but also to make them self-reliant,” he said. item.title: ULAB moves closer to joint PhD program with Portsmouth
item.description:
The University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) has moved closer to offering a joint PhD program with the University of Portsmouth (UoP), United Kingdom, following the soft launch of the initiative online on August 6.
The 1-hour-and-50-minute program, conducted through Zoom, brought together senior officials and academics from ULAB and UoP, along with project partners and representatives involved in quality assurance and international engagement.
The event began with welcome remarks by Prof Shamsad Mortuza, vice chancellor of ULAB. Bobby Mehta, pro vice-chancellor (Global Engagement) of UoP, and Jacqueline Priego, associate dean (Global Engagement) of UoP, represented the university.
ULAB was represented by Prof Jude William R Genilo, pro vice-chancellor.
Other participants included Md Musharoff Hossain, founder president of the Federation of Bangladesh Human Resource Organizations (FBHRO), as a project partner, and Piers Wall of the Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education (QAA), UK.
Prof Shahnaj Husne Jahan, head of the GED Department at ULAB; Jaina Hunt, UK-side liaison; and Parvez Mahmud, project director on the ULAB side, also attended the event.
Following the initial speeches, an interactive workshop on Transnational Education (TNE) was held. Participants were divided into 2 groups to discuss questions related to TNE and share their experiences and recommendations on developing the proposed joint PhD program.
At the end of the discussions, Prof Jude William R Genilo and Jacqueline Priego presented a summary of the key issues, suggestions and recommendations raised by the 2 groups.
The soft launch marks a milestone in ULAB's efforts to expand international partnerships and develop opportunities for advanced research and doctoral education.
The proposed collaboration with UoP aims to strengthen academic and research links between Bangladesh and the UK while creating opportunities for doctoral education through TNE.

item.description:
ACI PLC has appointed Tanvir Shahriar Rimon as director of ACI Properties Limited, one of the group's newest ventures and the company behind the flagship brand Sereno Levande.
He will lead the company's strategic direction, business growth, and transformation as ACI Properties advances its vision of building Bangladesh's most trusted technology-enabled property ecosystem through Sereno Levande.
With more than 23 years in Bangladesh's corporate sector, Tanvir has built a distinguished career across the real estate and marine fisheries industries, marked by business transformation, sustainable development, and customer-centric innovation.
He has contributed to the delivery of more than a thousand homes while leading large multidisciplinary organizations through sustained growth and operational excellence.
Previously, he served as executive director at Rancon Group and CEO of its real estate and sea fishing division, leading four companies across both sectors.
There, he transformed business performance and strengthened governance.
The real estate business achieved remarkable commercial growth and operational efficiency while earning industry recognition for its commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
In marine fisheries, he led pioneering initiatives including Bangladesh's first export of onboard block-frozen Ocean Tiger shrimp to Europe and a cold storage facility powered entirely by renewable energy.
A passionate advocate of ESG principles and green construction, Tanvir is also an author, leadership mentor, and educator, most recently serving as adjunct associate professor at Chittagong Independent University.
He founded the Connect the Dots Foundation during the Covid-19 pandemic, establishing a nationwide oxygen bank, and was honored as a Covid Hero by Rotary International in 2021.
He is a life fellow of the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB) and a member of the ESG Business Institute.
Recently launched, ACI Properties Limited was founded to create an integrated, technology-driven property services platform.
Through Sereno Levande, the company offers five integrated verticals under one platform: digital marketplace, property management, premium resale, serviced apartments, and corporate housing.
Designed around trust, transparency, and personalized care, Sereno Levande serves homeowners, tenants, investors, corporate clients, embassies, high commissions, and Non-Resident Bangladeshis, redefining how people experience property ownership.
Speaking on his appointment, Tanvir Shahriar Rimon said: "I am honored to lead ACI Properties at such an exciting stage. Through Sereno Levande, our vision is to redefine property services in Bangladesh by combining technology, trust, and operational excellence into one integrated platform. This journey is about creating lasting value for customers, empowering communities, and contributing to Bangladesh's sustainable urban future."
The appointment marks a significant milestone for ACI Properties as it builds a modern, service-driven property platform guided by its brand promise, "Living, Harmonized."

item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said that the opposition is now using the same language that ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina once used.

“We have an opposition party. Unfortunately, this opposition has once again started playing the same role as before. Hasina used to say, ‘We won’t allow this, we won’t let that happen’—they are speaking in the same language,” Mirza Fakhrul said.

He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at an event at the Rangpur District Shilpakala Academy at around 1:30 pm on Sunday.

The event was organised by US-based charity organisation Love Share BD to inaugurate its self-funded project aimed at helping disadvantaged people become self-reliant. As part of the initiative, 25 tea stalls were handed over to 25 disadvantaged people in the Rangpur region.

Mirza Fakhrul reminded the audience that the government was only four to five months old and had already undertaken a number of initiatives during this period.

Dwelling further on the country’s energy situation, Mirza Fakhrul said Bangladesh had to import oil and gas by ship, costing billions of dollars.

Speaking about the gas crisis, he said Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (BAPEX), which explores for oil and gas through drilling wells, had previously been left dysfunctional but was now being revived.

“Tenders have been invited for foreign companies to explore for gas here, and those companies are now coming,” he said.

Dwelling further on the country’s energy situation, Mirza Fakhrul said Bangladesh had to import oil and gas by ship, costing billions of dollars. He claimed that the Iran-US conflict had caused Bangladesh losses of nearly $4 billion in making payments.

“Even then, nobody has gone without oil or gas for a single day. Supplies have declined, but we are still getting them,” he said.

Speaking about plans for Rangpur and the northern region, Mirza Fakhrul said the prime minister wanted to develop agro-based industries in the region, which would create employment opportunities.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives MinisterWhen the BNP comes to government, you support the Jatiya Party. When the BNP comes to government, you support Jamaat. Then how will it work? How will you get [development]?

“This will create jobs. We will have work and won’t remain unemployed,” he said.

Referring to Rangpur's development, he said people in the region had historically remained behind because they had not always made the right political choices.

“When the BNP comes to government, you support the Jatiya Party. When the BNP comes to government, you support Jamaat. Then how will it work? How will you get [development]?” he remarked.

Mirza Fakhrul also said the government had established democracy, Parliament was functioning, and people had the freedom to speak, while newspapers could now publish whatever they wanted. However, he questioned the accuracy of information circulating on social media.

Among those present at the event were former Bangladesh ambassador to the United States and Senior Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Mushfiqul Fazal Ansari, Rangpur Development Authority Chairman Md Shamsuzzaman Samu, Rangpur City Corporation Administrator Saiful Islam and Love Share BD Director Zahid Khan.

Indigenous Peoples’ Day: Calls for constitutional recognition, legal rights
item.description:
On International Indigenous Peoples ' Day, the Bangladesh Adivasi Forum has demanded that the government take concrete steps to guarantee the constitutional , cultural, land, and legal rights of the country's indigenous communities.
A discussion meeting, public rally, and cultural program marking International Indigenous Peoples ' Day were held on Sunday at the Central Shaheed Minar in the capital.
Special guests at the event included human rights and women's rights activist Khushi Kabir; former member of parliament and vice president of the Parbatya Chittagong Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS), Ushatan Talukder; an educationist and former Dhaka University professor; Executive Director of Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB), Dr Iftekharuzzaman; a member of the Central Standing Committee of Bangladesh Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD); Executive Director of Manusher Jonno Foundation, Shaheen Anam; Executive Director of ALRD, Shamsul Huda; the Acting General Secretary of the Bangladesh Hindu-Buddhist-Christian Unity Council; General Secretary of the Communist Party of Bangladesh, Abdullah Al Kafi Ratan; Co-General Secretary of Bangladesher Samajtantrik Dal, Rajekuzzaman Ratan; writer and journalist Sohrab Hasan; Bangladesh Supreme Court lawyer Sara Hossain; Dhaka University teacher Robaet Ferdous; and a writer and researcher, among many others.
Indigenous people attend a cultural program, gathering and rally organized by the Bangladesh Indigenous Forum at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka on Sunday to mark International Day of the World`s Indigenous Peoples 2026. Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
In his welcome address, Sanjeeb Drong, general secretary of the Bangladesh Adivasi Forum, said: "For three decades now, we have been campaigning for indigenous peoples ' right to self-determination. More than four million indigenous people live in Bangladesh. We believe the Bangladeshi state must grant them constitutional recognition to protect their language, identity, land, culture, and self-identity."
He added: "The coexistence of different ethnic communities is what makes Bangladesh rich in linguistic, cultural, and traditional diversity — and that diversity is our country's beauty and strength. To protect indigenous peoples ' language, culture, and heritage, we must stop seizing and evicting them from their land in the name of development. At the same time, the state must take effective steps to secure their land and cultural rights ."
Indigenous people attend a cultural program, gathering and rally organized by the Bangladesh Indigenous Forum at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka on Sunday to mark International Day of the World`s Indigenous Peoples 2026. Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
Ushatan Talukder said Bangladesh is a country of many languages, many cultures, and many ethnic identities — and that diversity is our national strength. Yet it is a sad truth that the indigenous peoples who form a vital part of this diversity still face crises and discrimination over constitutional recognition, land rights , language, culture, and identity. Fifty-five years after independence, many of their basic rights remain unfulfilled.
He further said that "collective ownership," the traditional indigenous system of land tenure, has been recognized under ILO Conventions 107 and 169, both of which serve as legal instruments for indigenous peoples . Bangladesh ratified ILO Convention 107 in 1972 but has never ratified or endorsed Convention 169. "I call on the government to properly implement Convention 107 and to take steps toward ratifying Convention 169," he said.
He noted that the CHT Peace Accord is nearing its 30th anniversary, yet no visible progress has been made toward its implementation. The current government has promised in its election manifesto to build a "rainbow nation" — a Bangladesh that respects diversity.
"We believe that promise will only be realized through the full implementation of the Chittagong Hill Tracts Accord, by granting constitutional recognition to indigenous peoples , and by protecting their rights to land, language, culture, and identity," he said.
Dr Iftekharuzzaman said Indigenous Peoples ' Day is not only for indigenous communities — it stands as a symbol of rights and dignity for all landless, marginalized, and oppressed people. "The Chittagong Hill Tracts Accord was signed with the state in 1997 to fulfil the self-determination rights of the hill people. But 29 years on, it still hasn't been fully implemented," he said.
He added that the Bangladesh Army could play a significant role in implementing the accord. "Just as the Bangladesh Army has made important contributions as a UN peacekeeping force in countries around the world, we hope it will similarly help establish peace, harmony, and stability within the country by supporting the accord's implementation."
He called on the army to play a positive and effective role in resolving the long-standing disputes in the Chittagong Hill Tracts peacefully and in fully implementing the accord.
Abdullah Al Kafi Ratan, general secretary of the Communist Party of Bangladesh, said that even decades after independence, the country's indigenous peoples remain deprived of their rightful entitlements. Although Bangladesh won independence in 1971 with the dream of a discrimination-free, equitable nation, equal rights for all communities have still not been secured.
"Our movement has always stood with the oppressed and the deprived. Our struggle will continue until we secure justice for indigenous peoples and all oppressed communities, and build a discrimination-free, democratic, humane Bangladesh," he said.
Indigenous people attend a cultural program, gathering and rally organized by the Bangladesh Indigenous Forum at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka on Sunday to mark International Day of the World`s Indigenous Peoples 2026. Ahadul Karim Khan/Dhaka Tribune
Khushi Kabir said the day is observed every year because of its special importance — it repeatedly reminds the state that indigenous communities exist in Bangladesh and that they, too, have their own rights , identity, and dignity. She said that recognizing indigenous peoples as distinct ethnic groups is one of the main ways to protect their language, culture, and heritage. At the same time, their right to self-determination over their land must be ensured — which is why constitutional and l egal recognition for indigenous peoples is so urgently needed.
In the absence of the Bangladesh Adivasi Forum's president, his written statement was read out by Trijinad Chakma, a PCJSS staff member. In it, he said: "On this International Indigenous Peoples ' Day, I want to say to indigenous people everywhere — the majority of indigenous communities in the hills and plains of Bangladesh today are living under threat to their very existence. Fifty-five years after independence, indigenous people in the Chittagong Hill Tracts continue to lose their land, and their human rights are being trampled daily under military rule and state oppression. The CHT Accord, signed on December 2, 1997, to resolve the problems of hill indigenous peoples , is now approaching 29 years — yet the government has shown no real will to fully implement it. The situation for plainland indigenous communities is even more precarious: eviction from land, violence against women, discrimination, and impunity have pushed them further and further into the margins. To overcome this reality, indigenous students and youth must carry the struggle forward with unbreakable unity and resolve, further consolidating the fight for indigenous rights ."

item.title: ‘We were left like nomads for 40 hours at Rome airport’
item.description:
Bangladeshi passengers on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Toronto endured a nearly 40-hour ordeal at Rome airport after a technical problem grounded their flight, with many claiming they were left stranded in the airport lounge due to visa restrictions.
“We spent 40 hours like nomads. Eight hours were spent inside the aircraft. We were then taken to the airport lounge and told we would be taken to a hotel. But passengers holding US and Canadian passports were taken to hotels, while we, the Bangladeshi passport holders, were left in the lounge,” passenger Shahjahan Alam said after arriving in Dhaka.
The flight landed in Dhaka at 12:24pm on Sunday, and passengers began disembarking around 1:30pm, many visibly exhausted.
“They did not value our passports at all. We could not even eat the food they provided. Overall, we spent nearly two days like nomads,” Shahjahan said. Another passenger, Anika, said they learned about the technical problem after three hours.
“We were kept inside the aircraft for another five hours before being allowed to disembark. An airline official later came and apologised,” she said. Anika said Bangladeshi passport holders were kept in the lounge while US and Canadian passport holders were accommodated in hotels.
“We spent 40 hours sitting on chairs. Biman and our embassy could have arranged accommodation for us as well. They even offered visas on arrival, but due to negligence by officials, we had to suffer so much,” she said.
Passenger Shafayat Hossain urged the government to strengthen the Bangladeshi passport.
“As there is a new government and everything is being renewed, we do not want to see the old faces at Biman and the embassy. Still, we thank the government for bringing us back,” he said.
Dhaka University teacher Sayem Rana also criticised the handling of the situation.
“What is the point of reporting on Biman? Where was the coordination? How could we spend so many hours sitting on chairs? We suffered tremendously, yet no one spoke up,” he said.
Mahmuda Talukdar, another passenger, said she was accommodated at a hotel because she held a Canadian passport.
“I was spared the ordeal because I had my young daughter with me. But those who remained at the airport suffered greatly,” she said.
Passengers said the ordeal was particularly difficult for elderly people and children, who had to sit on chairs or sleep on the floor. They urged Biman to improve its services, warning that the national flag carrier could face serious consequences if such problems continue.
Biman flight BG306 departed Toronto for Dhaka on Thursday with 259 passengers. It made a scheduled stop at Rome airport for refuelling, where a technical problem was detected.
After an eight-hour effort failed to resolve the problem, the flight was cancelled and passengers were disembarked. Biman authorities subsequently arranged accommodation for some passengers at hotels and others in the airport lounge.
An engineering team carrying the necessary parts and equipment arrived in Rome at around 11:15pm Bangladesh time on Saturday. The team repaired the aircraft, making it fit for flight.
As the aircraft remained grounded for an extended period and many passengers were unable to leave the airport due to visa restrictions imposed by Italian immigration authorities, they were forced to remain at the airport.
Passengers alleged that they were kept inside the aircraft for nearly eight hours after landing in Rome before being informed about the technical problem. Several children, elderly passengers and those who were ill reportedly became unwell during the prolonged wait.

item.title: Job market is changing—should you change your decision?
item.description:
After completing their higher secondary examinations, every student faces a major question: What subject should I study, and what path should I take to build my career?

It may seem that this one decision will determine the course of their entire life. Finding the answer to this question is now more complicated than ever before. That is because technology, particularly artificial intelligence or AI, is rapidly changing the way we work, learn and think.

There is one important point to keep in mind. Students enrolling in university today will graduate in about four years. During this period, AI-powered technologies will bring major changes to the workplace.

According to the World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2025, 170 million new jobs will be created globally by 2030. At the same time, around 92 million jobs will disappear. This means there will be a net increase of approximately 78 million jobs.

The same report shows that, in percentage terms, the fastest-growing occupations will be led by big data specialists, with growth of 110 per cent, followed by fintech engineers at 90 per cent and AI and machine learning specialists at 82 per cent.

Technology will change, and the nature of professions will change as well. But the desire to learn, the willingness to acquire new skills and the ability to adapt to change—these three qualities will never become outdated.

Next are software and application developers at 57 per cent, security management specialists at 53 per cent, and data analysts and scientists at 41 per cent, it added.

According to the report, this list makes it clear that demand will not rise only for one particular profession; rather, the need for skills related to technology, information security and data will all increase in the coming years. The pace of this transformation is so rapid that it is difficult to say with certainty what the job market of the future will look like.

Best seller historian Yuval Noah Harari has said, “For the first time in human history, nobody knows for certain what the job market will look like 20 or 30 years from now.”

Therefore, it is important to keep in mind that the reality of the subject you want to study today may not be the same four years from now.

That is why the importance of fields such as computer science, data science, software engineering and information technology will increase further in the coming years. At the same time, demand for skilled professionals in areas such as machine learning, robotics, cybersecurity and the Internet of Things (IoT) will also grow rapidly. For those interested in mathematics, logic and statistics, these fields could be particularly promising.

However, one point needs to be made clear: AI is not merely a subject for computer science. The use of AI technology is growing in almost every field, including business, medicine, agriculture, law and journalism. AI-powered document analysis in law, data-driven crop-yield forecasting in agriculture and the use of AI in medical diagnosis are examples of this trend. Therefore, regardless of what someone studies, becoming familiar with technology and acquiring the ability to use it effectively is now almost essential.

Yuval Noah Harari, Best seller historianFor the first time in human history, nobody knows for certain what the job market will look like 20 or 30 years from now.

In the future, technological proficiency will be considered a supporting skill in every profession. Alongside their core field of study, students should therefore acquire basic knowledge of data analysis, programming or other technology-related areas.

This raises the question: How can we prepare for an AI-driven future? First, instead of fearing AI-related technologies, we need to become familiar with them and learn how to use them effectively. Second, we need to develop skills that AI cannot easily replicate, such as leadership, effective communication, creative thinking, problem-solving and the ability to build relationships with people. Third, we need to move away from the idea that learning ends once formal education is completed and develop a mindset of lifelong learning.

Futurist Alvin Toffler said long ago, “The illiterate of the 21st century will not be those who cannot read and write, but those who cannot learn, unlearn and relearn.”

In this era of rapid technological change, we will need to learn something new four years from now, and we will need to do so again 10 years from now. Therefore, the ability to learn will be the greatest qualification for the future.

I would also make an appeal to parents. Instead of putting excessive pressure on children and pushing them toward a particular subject, help them develop the ability to adapt to change. In the long run, giving greater importance to a child’s genuine interests, abilities and willingness to learn than to examination results or social expectations will produce better outcomes.

In conclusion, when choosing a field of study, the wisest approach is not to be overwhelmed by uncertainty but to strike a balance among one’s interests, abilities and the realities of the future.

Technology will change, and the nature of professions will change as well. But the desire to learn, the willingness to acquire new skills and the ability to adapt to change—these three qualities will never become outdated. In the AI-driven world of tomorrow, the students who begin preparing for this today will be the ones who stay ahead.

item.title: What the PM says at meeting with Hefazat ameer and senior leaders
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a meeting with Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh Ameer Allama Shah Mohibullah Babunagari and other senior leaders of the organisation in Fatikchhari, Chattogram, on Sunday afternoon.

During the meeting, he urged Hefazat to continue working with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), as it had done previously.

The meeting took place at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Uloom Babunagar Madrasah in Fatikchhari.

The prime minister arrived at Matarbari in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, in the morning before distributing relief supplies in Banshkhali. He then travelled by helicopter to Fatikchhari. After the helicopter landed at Pelagazi Dighi field, local party leaders and activists welcomed him. He then travelled by road to the Babunagar madrasah, with thousands of people lining both sides of the road to greet him.

Upon arriving at the madrasah, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman embraced Hefazat Ameer Allama Shah Mohibullah Babunagari and asked for his prayers.

Asked about the meeting, Hefazat-e-Islam Joint Secretary General Azizul Haque Islamabadi told Prothom Alo, “The prime minister told us that just as we stood with them before the election, we should continue to do so. I told him, ‘You should remain steadfast for Islam and the country; we are with you.’”

He added that the government had been able to manage the situation during Ramadan, but soon after it ended, tensions between Iran and the United States began in the Middle East, putting pressure on the country's economy, including oil and energy supplies.

The Hefazat leader said the organisation also submitted a written nine-point set of demands to the prime minister.

Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, State Minister for Land and Chattogram Hill Tracts Affairs Mir Mohammad Helal, State Minister for Energy Aninda Islam Amit, and members of parliament Sarwar Alam and Gias Quader Chowdhury were present at the meeting.

After the meeting, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed a gathering on the madrasah premises.

“I had promised Huzur before the election that I would come. The day after we formed the government, Ramadan began. The ‘head of fascism’ may have fled, but many remnants of fascism remained. Some people tried to take advantage of the situation during Ramadan,” he said.

He added that the government had been able to manage the situation during Ramadan, but soon after it ended, tensions between Iran and the United States began in the Middle East, putting pressure on the country's economy, including oil and energy supplies.

Prime MInister Tarique RahmanDuring the previous election, we worked together and saved the country from danger. Those of you who are here, our colleagues, worked alongside us. As a result, we were able to protect the country from a crisis.

“During the previous election, we worked together and saved the country from danger. Those of you who are here, our colleagues, worked alongside us. As a result, we were able to protect the country from a crisis,” he said.

“However, I want to make one thing clear: the problem is not over. During the previous fascist regime, you saw how the country's wealth and resources were looted and siphoned abroad,” he added.

Speaking about the ongoing gas crisis across the country, the prime minister said the situation would improve within the next five to seven days.

“Insha Allah, by the grace of Allah, the situation will be resolved within the next five to seven days. The problem will ease somewhat. We know there is also a power crisis. The people of this country are now paying the price for the unplanned measures taken during the fascist period,” he said.

Tarique Rahman also warned of attempts to spread confusion and create disorder.

“Please note that for the past few days there have been attempts to spread confusion and create disorder. That is why I am saying that just as we worked together before the election, we want to remain together in the days ahead,” he said.

Referring to Hefazat's nine-point demands, he added, “We will try to implement the demands you have presented gradually.”

The prime minister said he had sought everyone's prayers so that the government could establish justice and do something meaningful for the people.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said, “Our prime minister is a deeply pious man. Our relationship with you is not political. Insha Allah, the relationship we have with you will remain. Please just pray that we can develop the country while maintaining peace and order.”

At the end of the programme, the Hefazat ameer prayed for the welfare of the prime minister and the country, including that Bangladesh remain free from its enemies.

After the meeting in Fatikchhari, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the graves of former Hefazat Ameers Allama Shah Ahmad Shafi and Allama Junaid Babunagari in Hathazari.

item.title: PM: None will be allowed to play with people’s fate
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday urged all democratic forces to stand united against those seeking to create disorder, spread confusion and obstruct the country’s development, saying none would be allowed to play with the fate of the people.
“Now is the time to build the country, now is the time to shape the destiny of the nation. Therefore, we have to turn the 40 crore hands of our 20 crore people into the hands of workers and take our country forward,” he said.
The prime minister said this while addressing a rehabilitation program for flood-affected people at Hatazari Government College ground on Sunday evening.
Highlighting the prevailing situation of the country, he said some political parties are spreading confusion and trying to obstruct the government’s development activities.
“Today, we have to make a decision. All democratic people of Bangladesh who believe in democracy and freedom of expression have to decide what steps we should take against those who want to create disorder, block roads by coming onto the streets and want to mislead people,” he said.
Calling upon the people to remain united against such attempts, Tarique Rahman said, “Let us take a pledge, let us take an oath that we must stand against those who want to jeopardize country’s development and progress, and are out to obstruct the way of improving the fate of the people.”
“Changing the fate of the people is our vision and mission. We will work, we will build the country, Bangladesh First (Korbo Kaj, Gorbo Desh, Sobar Agee Bangladesh),” he said.
“BNP firmly believes that people are the source of all political power. Since the people have lent their support to BNP, it’s our sacred responsibility to implement the party’s 31-point development goal,” he said.
Terming BNP’s 31-point development goal as the people’s program, the prime minister said: “BNP would take the country forward by overcoming all obstacles to fulfill the aspirations of the people. The party will continue working to change the fate of the people and transform the country into a developed one.”
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed also spoke on the occasion.

item.title: PM urges Islamic scholars to stay united to maintain peace, stability
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday urged Islamic scholars (alem-ulema) to work with the government and remain united in the days to come to maintain peace and stability amid various plots to destabilise the country.
Speaking at a views-exchange meeting with Islamic scholars at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Ulum Babunagar Madrasha in Fatikchhari upazila, he said BNP’s political opponents in the 13th parliamentary election are trying to create disorder and spread confusion in the country.
“We saw it in 1991 and 1996. You also saw during the last election that you and we worked together against those who wanted to take the country in a different direction. Over the past few days, they have again been trying to spread various messages of confusion and create disorder,” Tarique said.
He said the government and the alem-uema and Islamic scholars worked together in the past and should continue to do so to keep the country on the right track.
“With the prayers of Huzur [Allama Shah Muhibullah], I want to request that we remain together in the coming days as well,” the prime minister said.
Referring to various demands raised by representatives of Qawmi madrashas, he said Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has already explained some of the issues and that the government would address them gradually.
“We have to understand that many other people also live in this country. We want to build a Bangladesh where its people and children can live well, earn a living and live in peace,” Tarique said.
He said people of different faiths should be able to practise their religions peacefully.
“We will practise our religion, and they will practise theirs. But as most people here are Muslims, we will also take Islam forward and take the country forward, InshaAllah,” the prime minister said.
Explaining his visit to the madrasha, Tarique said he has come mainly to pay his respects and seek the prayers of Allama Shah Muhibullah Babunagari.
He also stressed the need to prevent attempts to create disorder, saying the government has important work to do in improving people’s lives.
“We have to create employment, improve healthcare and education, repair roads, schools and colleges, and fix bridges and culverts in different places,” Tarique said.
The prime minister said peace and stability are essential for attracting both domestic and foreign investment.
“If there is disorder in the country, foreign investors who want to invest here will not come. If there is no disorder, they will invest. Then our children and family members will get opportunities for jobs,” he said.
Tarique said ensuring people’s wellbeing is the government’s responsibility and sought prayers so that the government could fulfil that responsibility. “ Allah has given us this responsibility, and we have formed the government. Pray that we can do something good for the welfare of people,” he said.
The prime minister also warned against attempts to spread confusion and create disorder, saying such activities could undermine the government's efforts to develop the country.
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed also spoke at the meeting.
Tarique had earlier met Hefazat-e-Islam chief Allama Shah Muhibullah Babunagari at the madrasha and enquired about his health.
Babunagari welcomed the prime minister on his arrival and held a meeting with him before the views-exchange session.
Hefazat-e-Islam Secretary General Sajidur Rahman placed their seven demands during the prime minister’s visit.

item.title: Govt mulls launching electric water buses around Dhaka
item.description:
The government is considering launching electric water buses along Dhaka’s 110-kilometre circular waterway as part of efforts to ease the capital’s chronic traffic congestion and develop an alternative public transport network.
Authorities are preparing a comprehensive plan and roadmap to revive passenger and tourist services along the waterway, which runs through the Buriganga, Turag, Shitalakkhya, Balu and Dhaleshwari rivers.
A meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office on July 1 decided to take coordinated measures to launch electric water bus services on the existing circular waterway within a month.
Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation (BIWTC) Chairman ATM Abdul Bari Danny said the authorities are preparing a roadmap to ensure the effective and organized operation of the proposed service.
“We have discussed the matter with the prime minister. We also discussed how the initiative can be operated in an efficient and well-organized manner. We are now preparing a final plan and roadmap, and we hope to operate it successfully in the future,” Danny told Dhaka Tribune.
Asked whether Bangladesh was considering solar-powered or electric vessels similar to those used in developed countries, Danny said electricity supply and utility-related matters fall under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources.
“The utility and electricity-related matters will be dealt with by the Ministry of Power. We cannot comment on this issue,” he said.
The proposed circular waterway stretches 110km around Dhaka, covering five rivers. Of the total route, 63km has a depth of 12 feet, while the remaining 47km has a depth of around eight feet. Conservation dredging is underway along a 10km stretch between Sirnichtek and Ashulia to increase its depth to 12 feet, while the remaining 37km is planned to be deepened gradually.
The waterway connects four river ports—Dhaka, Narayanganj, Tongi and Mirkadim—and has five terminals and nine landing stations, with 45 terminal and landing points in total.
Talking to Dhaka Tribune, Buet transport expert Dr Md Hadiuzzaman said the circular waterway could only succeed if lessons from the previous initiative were addressed through a professionally prepared, integrated and institutionally coordinated plan.
“The new system should provide reliable feeder services, ensure frequent peak-hour operations, regulate vessel and cross-river traffic, and improve river water and environmental conditions,” he said.
The government is also looking to involve private operators in reviving the waterway.
At a July 9 meeting at the Ministry of Shipping, authorities decided to hold discussions with private entrepreneurs interested in operating commercial public transport on the Gabtoli-Sadarghat route.
BIWTA was asked to consult stakeholders and interested entrepreneurs and determine the next course of action.
At another meeting on July 14, BIWTA discussed high-speed launches and speedboats, passenger catamarans and tourist vessels with interested owners and operators.
Participants stressed the need to free Dhaka’s surrounding rivers from encroachment and pollution, establish modern landing stations, improve road connections and ensure adequate public transport links. Passenger safety was also identified as a priority.
Professor Dr Ainun Nishat, adviser at the Centre for Climate Change and Environmental Research, said Dhaka’s inland waterways still have significant potential to ease traffic congestion.
He called for greater private-sector involvement, saying the government should focus on regulation, monitoring and accountability rather than directly managing every aspect of the system.
Nishat also criticised what he described as “projectitis” in Bangladesh’s development administration.
“Projectitis is a major problem in our development system. Ministries often become more interested in taking up projects than actually getting the work done. Once this unnecessary project-driven approach stops, real development can begin,” he said.
He said reviving waterways does not necessarily require mega projects, but rather targeted dredging, correction of sharp bends and regular maintenance.
Water bus services were launched on the Badamtoli-Gabtoli route on August 28, 2010 and the Narayanganj-Tongi route on November 22, 2014. Both services were eventually suspended due to financial losses—in September 2019 and March 2020 respectively.
A total of 12 water buses were constructed at a cost of Tk9.20 crore. According to BIWTC data, they generated Tk2.52 crore in revenue against expenditure of Tk37.87 crore, resulting in a loss of Tk35.35 crore.
The official assessment cited shorter road travel times, Buriganga pollution, traffic congestion around Sadarghat, poor connectivity to landing stations and inadequate infrastructure among the reasons for the service’s failure. Sand-carrying vessels also prevented water buses from maintaining their expected speed.
River pollution remains a major challenge. A recent BIWTA survey identified 424 outlets discharging liquid waste into rivers surrounding Dhaka, including 244 associated with privately owned factories and industrial establishments.
Authorities have decided to identify pollution points and ensure proper collection and disposal of waste generated by vessels.
Nishat said Dhaka’s waterway network must also be redesigned in line with changing transport technologies.
“We are entering the era of electric vehicles and modern transport technologies. We cannot build a new transport system with old ideas. Long-term planning, efficient management and private-sector expertise are essential to make Dhaka’s waterways viable,” he said.
The government is also considering smaller and more frequent vessels to reduce passenger waiting times.
The circular waterway already has 20km of completed walkway, while another 52km is under construction with 92% progress. A further 100km has been proposed.
Authorities have installed 6,320 boundary pillars against a target of 7,100. Between 2009 and 2024, 17,829 illegal structures were removed under Dhaka River Port, recovering 519.04 acres of riverbank land. Another 6,963 illegal structures were removed under Narayanganj River Port, recovering 316.06 acres.
The success of the new initiative will ultimately depend not merely on putting electric vessels on the water, but on integrating waterways with road transport, ensuring reliable landing facilities, maintaining navigability, controlling pollution and providing an affordable and efficient service.
